full_judgment:
7. Mr. Abdus Samad, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the proposed amendment would change the nature and character of the suit. He further submits that the court cannot stop the enactment of the bank guarantee. According to him, by the proposed amendment the plaintiff wanted to add some prayers which are barred by the provision of limitation and such prayer at belated stage has been brought only to delay the disposal of the suit. In reply to the submission made by Mr. A Samad, Mr Mahbubuddin, learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff-opposite parties, submits that by the proposed amendment there is no chance of changing the nature and character of the suit. The instant prayers for an injunction, direction and enforcement contract are interspersed and supplementary' to the original prayers and relevant with the facts and circumstances of the case. For proper and final adjudication of the matter and to resolve the real question in controversy between the parties the proposed amendment was necessary. 

 9. In the case of Bhagwanji Morarji Gouldas vs Aelmgic Chemical Works Co. Ltd and others reported in AIR 1948 (PC) 100 it was observed that amendment of the plaint introducing a new claim which would have been barred by limitation, at the time when the leave was sought cannot be allowed. There is a limitation on the wide power of the court to amend the pleading where the application for amendment introduces a new claim as made at a belated stage cannot be allowed causing injury and injustice to the other side. In the absence of special circumstances, plaintiff will not be allowed to amend his plaint by introducing a cause of action which since the date of the plaint has become time barred. In the case of Radhika Debi vs Bajrangi Singh reported in AIR 1996 (SC) 2358 has discouraged to allow the time barred prayer. In that case filing written statement in a suit for partition the defendant stated about a deed of gift in there favour. But the plaintiff filed application for amendment plaint seeking relief against the said deed of gift three years thereafter. It was held that the plaintiff was not entitled to amend the plaint because of no steps having been taken in 3 years to amend the plaint. The accrued right in favour of the defendant would be defeated by permitting the amendment of the plaint. Issuing the impugned letter dated 15-5-89 the defendant had abandoned the agreement dated 7-4-84 that is, there was a definite cause of action to file the suit for specific performance of contract. The specified limitation is 3 years from the date of refusal. Furthermore, it appears that the original suit was for declaration that certain letter is illegal and for permanent injunction but by the proposed amendment the plaintiffs sought for a decree for specific performance of contract, that is, the plaintiffs want to convert the suit of one character into suit of another character and to substitute one distinct cause of action depriving the other party of the right acquired by lapse of time and, in effect, take away the right. Making an agreement to purchase the property the plaintiff No. 1 took delivery of possession of the same and has been enjoying the same depriving Government from huge amount.
